title.narrative: Life-saving and safe return: Integrating Protection and WASH for the most vulnerable displaced, returnees and host communities in Rural Damascus, (Babila, bahdaliyah), Aleppo (Jabal Samaan, Salheen).

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtTerre des Hommes Foundation (Tdh) is implementing a 12-month integrated intervention to address the interconnected challenges of child protection and water access in vulnerable communities across Rural Damascus (Babila, severity 4, PiN 189,357 – 14% returnees, 25% IDPs).) and Aleppo (Jabal Samaan severity 3, PiN 1,346,113 – 27% returnees, 1% IDPs). This comprehensive response targets displaced populations, returnees, and host communities facing acute humanitarian needs exacerbated by years of conflict and economic instability in Babila, Bahdaliyah and Jabal Samaan, Salheen.ltbrgtOngoing displacements and returnee movements since December 2024 have strained services and protection mechanisms, escalating humanitarian needs—particularly child protection risks—due to eroded livelihoods and lack of access to WASH, shelter, food and other essential services. ltbrgtTdh conducted needs assessment in June 2025 through focus group discussions and key informant interviews with community leaders, water authorities, and affected populations, it revealed multiple protection risks stemming from economic hardship and water insecurity. School dropout rates among children have reached alarming levels, with many forced to abandon education to support their families through labor for boys and early marriage for girls. The economic strain on households has led to deteriorating mental health among children and their caregivers and increasing incidents of domestic violence. Social tensions between displaced populations, returnees, and host communities continue to escalate due to competition over limited resources and services. The assessment documented widespread reliance on unsafe water sources, with families forced to either purchase water at exorbitant prices or undertake long, hazardous journeys to collect water. This water crisis directly compounds existing vulnerabilities, particularly for children and women.ltbrgtTdh's response is grounded in international humanitarian standards, including the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Child Protection Minimum Standards. The intervention adopts a multi-sectoral approach that simultaneously addresses immediate survival needs while building longer-term resilience and ensure safe and dignified return:ltbrgt1. Child Protection ServicesltbrgtThe project establishes comprehensive child protection services including mental health and psychosocial support for 1,000 children exhibiting signs of distress, parenting programs to strengthen 500 caregiver capacities, and targeted case management for 150 children at highest risk. Community-based awareness initiatives will promote children's rights and positive coping mechanisms targeting 3,000 individuals.ltbrgt2. Community Protection SystemsltbrgtRecognizing that sustainable protection requires local ownership, the intervention focuses on capacity-building through the establishment of two community-based protection committees and two youth clubs. These committees will lead efforts to mitigate protection risks, resolve social conflicts, and promote social cohesion between different population groups through provision of 6 community initiatives to promote the peace coexistence, also Tdh will conduct four protection monitoring assessments, to identify and analyse key protection risks, trends, and rights violations affecting children and their communities.ltbrgt3. Water System RehabilitationltbrgtThe WASH component prioritizes sustainable solutions to the water crisis through rehabilitation of critical infrastructure targeting 135,000 individuals in both areas. By repairing damaged water networks with durable materials, the project will restore reliable access to safe water, directly reducing protection risks associated with water collection while improving overall community health.ltbrgtThis project will contribute to not only meet urgent humanitarian needs of the displaced population but also lay foundations for safe, dignified and sustainable reintegration of the returnees.ltbrgtlt/pgt
